exposure: presence of proteinuria in mothers with preeclampsia
cohort: The study included 816 pregnant patients diagnosed with preeclampsia (PE) at a tertiary care center in Brazil between January 2015 and December 2019.
finding: The presence of proteinuria in mothers with preeclampsia is associated with significantly worse neonatal outcomes (fetal growth restriction, low birth weight, ICU admission, preterm birth), but no significant differences in maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: No significant differences were observed in C-section rates between mothers with and without proteinuria.
